claim.text: stone marten density, individuals per km2 (abstract)
claim.fixed_at: targets.csv, committed 2026-10-30 before any run (private repo 456e98d)

inputs.what: authors' code and data (GitHub release archived on Zenodo)

changes: path only: one setwd() line commented out (changes.diff, 4 lines, kept with the run files)

environment.jags: 4.3.2, built from official source (hashes match), because rjags 4.17 needs JAGS 4 and Homebrew ships 5

command: python3 -I run_paper.py data/papers/093/run script.R (runs Rscript script.R, 24 h limit)

attempts: 1: stopped at once, rstan missing (dependency scan had read only the main script)
2: cut off by my own session ending, partway through chain 1; no result
run.mcmc: 3 chains x 50,000 iterations after 10,000 burn-in, no fixed seed; Rhat <= 1.001 for all monitored parameters

comparison.tolerance: PLAN.md: within 5% of the estimate or 10% of the reported interval's width, whichever is larger; SD-only means the interval is +/-1.96 SD. Here max(0.0176, 0.0318) = 0.0318
comparison.checks: psi (data-augmentation inclusion) 0.154, far from 1, so the M=500 ceiling isn't binding; N 76.5 (48 to 115)

status: reproduced only by running their code
does_not_show: an independent check: I re-ran the authors' own code; I didn't compute density another way
that the model suits the system (spatial capture-recapture assumptions, the 2 km buffer, how the four collared animals are matched to capture rows: notes/093-model.md)
that the data are sound, or are what the paper describes
that the paper's other results reproduce: only this one number was checked (Kellner et al.'s note says some models in the paper seem missing from the code)
that it would reproduce with other package versions or on another machine
that stone marten density in the study area is 0.35 per km2
notes: Mean 0.329 vs published 0.352: a difference of 0.023, inside the 0.032 tolerance. MCMC with no fixed seed, so a re-run will differ slightly. First comparison in this pilot.
